Currently handling smaller handyman and home improvement jobs (wood rot, drywall/wall repair, interior/exterior painting, electrical & plumbing fixtures, landscape lighting, flooring, finish carpentry, door/window repair).

additionalNotes: Primary Color (#1C3144 - Deep Navy / Slate): Black can feel harsh or unapproachable on digital screens. Deep slate navy projects stability, structural strength, and high-end craftsmanship. It grounds the website while feeling more premium than standard black.
Secondary (#A23B2A - Warm Brick / Terracotta): Evokes traditional masonry, warm wood tones, and architectural materials. It bridges the gap between rugged construction and refined residential design.

Tertiary (#F4F6F8 - Crisp Off-White / Architectural Light Grey): Pure white (#FFFFFF) can feel clinical. A soft, cool off-white acts as a clean background for high-res project galleries without straining the eyes.

Accent 1 (#D00000 - Firehouse Red / First Responder Accent): A subtle nod to Nicholas's background as a Bluffton firefighter. Used sparingly on action buttons (e.g., 'Get Free Consultation' or 'Realtor 10% Discount'), it commands immediate attention and builds immediate community trust.

Accent 2 (#E0A96D - Lowcountry Oak / Natural Wood Tone): Perfectly reflects GEA's focus on finish carpentry, decks, doors, and custom kitchen/bath trim. Connects the digital brand to the physical materials Nick uses every day.

GEA Typography: Uses a high-contrast, classic Serif font (similar to Cinzel or Times New Roman). Serif fonts convey tradition and prestige, but this specific font feels disjointed when paired with the modern, geometric rooflines above it.
Construction LLC. Typography: Uses a Geometric Sans-Serif font (similar to Montserrat or Century Gothic).

The Mismatch Issue: Combining a traditional serif on 'GEA' with a modern sans-serif on 'Construction LLC.' creates visual friction. In the construction and remodeling space, typographic unity signifies precision and structural integrity.

Header Font: Montserrat (All-Caps / Bold Weights for Brand Headings)Visual Match: Montserrat directly matches the clean, geometric structure of 'Construction LLC.' in the current logo.  Its wide stance and heavy geometric proportions project strength, reliability, and modern architectural design. Standardizing 'GEA CONSTRUCTION' into a bold, clean sans-serif like Montserrat unifies the logo mark with website headers (H1, H2, H3).

Body Font: Open Sans - Highly legible on mobile devices, which is critical for real estate agents and homeowners checking services on their phones.  It is a Neutral Complement - Open Sans is clean and unpretentious—it lets the project portfolio photos and service details take center stage without competing with bold headers.
